title: Customizing your site
text:
Source: vignettes/customizing.qmd
If you want to customize your site, you can do so by editing _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, which quartodown::use_quartodown() creates. The _quartodown/ folder at the package root also holds the files that style the site. _quartodown.yml has nine fields, all optional:

title: Customizing your site
text:
The reference index
Without reference:, the index lists every function in one section. To group them, list the sections:
reference:
1  - title: Read and write
2    desc: Functions for getting data in and out.
    contents:
3      - read_data
4      - starts_with("write_")
  - title: Helpers
5    subtitle: Low-level
    contents:
      - has_concept("helpers")
6      - -internal_helper

1

Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.

2

Optional Markdown text, shown under the heading.

3

A topic, by any of its \alias{} names or its Rd file name.

4

A selector.

5

An optional heading one level below title.

6

A leading - removes a topic.


The selectors are:







Selector
Selects topics




starts_with("x"), ends_with("x"), contains("x")
with an alias that starts with, ends with or contains x


matches("regex")
with an alias matching a regular expression


has_concept("x"), has_keyword("x")
with that \concept{} or \keyword{}


c(...)
selected by any of the selectors given


- before a topic or selector
removed from those the entries above select, or as the first entry, from all topics



Topics that no section lists get a warning and are left off the index. The exception is \keyword{internal} topics, which are left out, without a page, unless named, as with roxygen’s reexports, or selected with internal = TRUE, as in starts_with("dev_", internal = TRUE).
The format is the same as pkgdown’s reference: field, so an existing one can be copied over.

title: Customizing your site
text:
The navbar
navbar: lists the items on the navbar’s left and right, in order. The default is:
navbar:
  left: [intro, reference, articles, news]
  right: [repo]
Each of these is a keyword that quartodown turns into an item, and leaves out if the package has nothing for it:







Keyword
Item




intro
“Get started”: the vignette named after the package, or the only top-level vignette if there’s just one


reference
“Reference”: the function reference index


articles
“Articles”: a menu of every vignette no other item links, top-level ones first, then those in subfolders


news
“Changelog”: NEWS.md


repo
The repository in DESCRIPTION’s URL, with a GitHub or GitLab icon (else a generic one)



Any other item is a vignette, given as its path relative to vignettes/ without extension and linked with its title, or a Quarto navbar item. Inside a Quarto item’s menu:, vignettes are given the same way, and a folder ending in / lists every vignette in it.
For example, with the vignettes in a folder for each menu:
navbar:
  left:
    - reference
    - news
    - text: Get started
      menu:
1        - get-started/installation
        - get-started/first-steps
    - text: User guide
2      menu: user-guide/
    - text: Developers
      menu:
        - dev/internals
3        - text: Contributing
          href: CONTRIBUTING.md
  right:
    - text: Blog
      href: https://example.com/blog
    - repo

1

vignettes/get-started/installation.qmd.

2

Every vignette in vignettes/user-guide/, sorted by file name.

3

Any Quarto navbar item works in a menu too.


Vignettes can live in any subfolder of vignettes/. Files and folders whose name starts with _ or . are skipped, as Quarto does.
Every vignette is built, even one the navbar doesn’t link to. Such a vignette can only be reached through links from other pages, so build_site() warns about it, unless the navbar has articles, which lists every vignette nothing else links.






Note



R only builds top-level vignettes into the package, so vignettes in subfolders are website-only.



A sidebar instead
With style: sidebar, the left items move into a sidebar beside every page, and the navbar keeps the site’s title, the search box and the right items:
navbar:
  style: sidebar
Menus become sections of the sidebar, and “Reference” lists every reference page by function name, with a section for each titled group of reference:.

title: Customizing your site
text:
The home page
The home page shows README.md, or, if there is none, the package’s description from DESCRIPTION. To give the site a different home page than the README, use home: file: at another file, relative to the package root:
home:
  file: index.qmd
It can be Markdown (.md) or a Quarto document (.qmd), whose code runs when the site is built, as in a vignette. Write links and image paths in it relative to the package root, as in the README.
Next to the page, a sidebar shows the package’s links, license, community files, citation, authors and badges. sidebar: can reorder its sections, drop some, or add your own, and links: adds to its links:
home:
  links:
    - text: Blog
      href: https://example.com/blog
  sidebar:
1    structure: [links, funding, license, authors]
    components:
2      funding:
        title: Funding
        text: Supported by [a grant](https://example.com).

1

The sections, in order. The built-in ones are links, license, community, citation, authors and dev (the README’s badges); by default, all of them in that order, then your own.

2

A section of your own: a heading and Markdown text.


For full control over the page you can turn the sidebar off with sidebar: false:
home:
  file: index.qmd
  sidebar: false
The page then shows the file as written. Like any other page, it then gets a table of contents, which toc: false in its front matter can turn off.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Authors
The home page’s sidebar and the footer list the authors with the roles aut, cre and fnd from DESCRIPTION’s Authors@R, and the authors page lists everyone. authors: can link a person’s name, or replace it with HTML such as a logo, and change who is shown:
authors:
1  Jane Doe:
    href: https://jane.example.com
  Acme Inc:
    href: https://acme.example.com
    html: <img src="https://acme.example.com/logo.png" alt="Acme" height="24">
  sidebar:
2    roles: [aut, cre]
3    after: Thanks to all [contributors](authors.html).
  footer:
    roles: [cre]
4    text: Maintained by

1

A person, by their name as in Authors@R.

2

The roles shown in the sidebar.

3

Markdown shown under the sidebar’s list, or with before: above it.

4

Instead of “Developed by”.


The format is the same as pkgdown’s authors:.

title: Customizing your site
text:
The repository
Source links (the “Source:” line under each page’s title), the sidebar’s “Browse source code”, the navbar’s repository icon and the changelog’s #123 and @user links all come from the first GitHub, GitLab (including self-hosted, if its host name has gitlab in it) or Codeberg URL in DESCRIPTION. For a package in a folder of a repository, give the URL of the folder, with its branch, as in https://github.com/me/repo/tree/main/mypkg.
repo: sets them where that isn’t enough, such as for another host or branch:
repo:
  url:
1    home: https://git.sr.ht/~me/mypkg
2    source: https://git.sr.ht/~me/mypkg/tree/main/item/
3    issue: https://todo.sr.ht/~me/mypkg/
4    user: https://sr.ht/~
5  branch: devel

1

The repository’s page.

2

Prefix of a file’s link, such as R/foo.R.

3

Prefix of an issue’s link, such as 123.

4

Prefix of a user’s link.

5

The branch the source links point to, instead of the default branch. Ignored when source: is set.


Each is optional and replaces only its own link. The format is the same as pkgdown’s repo:.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Redirects
When a page moves, such as a function’s reference page after it is renamed you can use redirects: so links to the old address keeps working. Each entry is a pair: the old address and the new one, both relative to the site’s root:
redirects:
  - ["reference/foo.bar.html", "reference/foo_bar.html"]
  - ["articles/old-guide.html", "vignettes/guide.html"]
For a vignette, Quarto’s own aliases: in its front matter does the same.

title: Customizing your site
text:
Other Quarto settings
quartodown writes a Quarto configuration into _quarto/_quarto.yml (overwritten on every build). The quarto: field is merged over it, key by key:

A list of entries, such as website: navbar: left:, is added to.
Any other value is replaced.
~ removes a setting.

For example, to fold code blocks, drop the table of contents and change the footer:
quarto:
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true
      toc: ~
  website:
    page-footer:
      right: "Built with love."
See the Quarto website reference for the full list of changes you can make.
quarto: applies to every page. To change a single vignette instead, set the option in its front matter, which overrides the site-wide value:
---
title: "A long tutorial"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
    toc-depth: 3
---
To change a single code chunk, use a chunk option such as #| code-fold: true.

title: Customizing your site
Customizing your site
text:
Coming from pkgdown
Moving a site over is very easy, and mostly means moving _pkgdown.yml’s settings into _quartodown/_quartodown.yml. These have the same format, so can be copied as is: url:, reference:, home: sidebar:, home: links:, authors:, repo: and redirects:. The rest maps as follows:



pkgdown
quartodown




navbar:
lists items differently; see The navbar


articles:
no equivalent: group vignettes with navbar menus instead


home: title:, title:
quarto: website: navbar: title:


home: description:
quarto: website: description:


lang:
quarto: lang:


template: bootswatch:
theme: light:


template: bslib:
_quartodown/extra.scss; fonts as below


template: opengraph:
quarto: website: open-graph: and twitter-card:, as below


template: includes:
quarto: format: html: include-in-header: etc.


template: math-rendering:
quarto: format: html: html-math-method:


template: params: ganalytics:
quarto: website: google-analytics:


template: light-switch:
always on: the site has a light and a dark theme


navbar: bg:, type:
theme: or _quartodown/extra.scss


toc: depth:
quarto: format: html: toc-depth:


figures:
quarto: format: html: fig-width:, fig-height:, fig-dpi:


footer:
authors: footer:, or quarto: website: page-footer:



A separate home page (an index.md used instead of the README) isn’t picked up automatically: set it with home: file:. Code that checks IN_PKGDOWN (or pkgdown::in_pkgdown()) should check identical(Sys.getenv("IN_QUARTODOWN"), "true") instead.
For example, this part of a _pkgdown.yml:
template:
  bootswatch: flatly
  bslib:
    base_font: {google: "Inter"}
    code_font: {google: "Fira Code"}
  opengraph:
    twitter:
      creator: "@me"
      card: summary_large_image
home:
  title: "mypkg: Do Things"
  description: A package that does things.
becomes, in _quartodown/_quartodown.yml:
theme:
  light: flatly
quarto:
  website:
    description: A package that does things.
    twitter-card:
      creator: "@me"
      card-style: summary_large_image
and, in _quartodown/extra.scss:
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter&family=Fira+Code&display=swap");
$font-family-sans-serif: "Inter", sans-serif;
$font-family-monospace: "Fira Code", monospace;
A custom navbar item, such as a link to CRAN, is a Quarto navbar item:
navbar:
  right:
    - repo
    - text: CRAN
      href: https://cran.r-project.org/package=mypkg
The rest works as with pkgdown, except that vignettes are published under vignettes/ rather than articles/: articles/foo.html becomes vignettes/foo.html, and articles/bar.html, from vignettes/articles/bar.Rmd, becomes vignettes/articles/bar.html. Likewise, the changelog is NEWS.html rather than news/index.html. Update links to them, or keep the old addresses working with redirects:.

title: Technical details
text:
Source: vignettes/articles/technical.qmd
quartodown generates a Quarto website project from the package sources, so the man pages, vignettes and generated pages are all Quarto pages, and every Quarto feature works.

title: Technical details
text:
How a build works
quartodown::build_site() runs in three stages:

Before rendering, it installs the package into a temporary library and writes a Quarto project into _quarto/.
During rendering, Quarto renders _quarto/ into docs/, running the examples and vignettes against that package.
After rendering, it links code to its documentation, adds hover tooltips and writes the redirect pages.

In an interactive session it then serves docs/ with preview_site(). The server keeps running for the rest of the session, so after a rebuild the open page reloads instead of a new one opening.
build_site(devel = TRUE) skips the install and loads the package from source with pkgload::load_all() instead. It is faster, but code that starts other R processes (for example with callr or parallel) won’t find the package, and build-stage \Sexpr{} macros in the man pages don’t run.
Throughout the build, the environment variable IN_QUARTODOWN is "true", so the package’s code can tell it is running for the site, and IN_QUARTODOWN_PKG is the package’s name.
_quarto/ is rewritten on every build, and gitignored by quartodown::use_quartodown(). To change the site, edit _quartodown/ instead (see Customizing your site).
_quarto/
├── _quarto.yml                   # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.qmd                     # home page
├── reference/
│   ├── index.qmd                 # function reference index
│   └── <topic>.qmd               # a page per man/*.Rd
├── authors.qmd                   # authors and citation page
├── vignettes/                    # the vignettes, as they are
├── man/figures/                  # images for the README and man pages
├── NEWS.md                       # changelog, with issues and users linked
├── _quartodown/                  # the package's _quartodown/, as it is
└── quartodown.scss               # theme on top of Quarto's HTML

title: Technical details
text:
The man pages
Each man/*.Rd file becomes a reference page, served at reference/<topic>.html. It is rendered with the package’s Rd macros (such as Rdpack’s \insertRef{}), and build-stage \Sexpr{} macros run with the package installed, as in R CMD build. Examples run, with their output in the same block as the code, prefixed with #>. To give a chunk’s output a block of its own, in a vignette too, set #| collapse: false on it.
If DESCRIPTION’s URL includes a GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg repository, each reference page and vignette links to its source file under the title.

title: Technical details
text:
Code links and tooltips
downlit links function calls in R code blocks, and inline code like mean(), to their documentation. docs/pkgdown.yml lets downlit on other sites link to your reference pages in turn.
That file needs the site’s address: url: in _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, or else the first URL in DESCRIPTION that isn’t a GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg repository.
References to the package’s own functions also get a hover tooltip with their usage and the first sentence of their description. build_site() warns when a first sentence is longer than 200 characters, since the tooltip cuts it off. To build without tooltips, use build_site(tooltips = FALSE).

title: Technical details
text:
The theme
The site uses Quarto’s default theme in light mode and darkly in dark mode, or the themes theme: picks, with quartodown.scss on top of each, and then _quartodown/extra.scss if the package has one. With the default light theme, quartodown-fonts.scss also gives the dark theme the same system fonts and heading sizes. The mode follows the browser’s preference.
Code output keeps the colors packages such as cli give it in a terminal, in shades that suit the light or dark theme.

title: quartodown
text:
quartodown is an R package that turns your package’s README, help pages and vignettes into a website, rendered entirely by Quarto.


Every page, help pages included, is a Quarto page, so you get:

every Quarto feature, from callouts and tabsets to code annotations and cross-references, on every page;
Quarto’s themes, extensions and settings.

On top of that, quartodown adds:

the package website layout R users know from pkgdown: a home page sidebar, a grouped function reference, articles and a changelog;
function links with hover tooltips.




Install the stable version from CRAN:
install.packages("quartodown")
or the development version from GitHub:
pak::pak("BjarkeHautop/quartodown")
quartodown also needs Quarto installed.



Browse the site to see how it looks! Quarto features shows callouts, tabsets, footnotes and more on a quartodown site. If you like what you see, and want to use it for your own package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, with a reference: field that lists your package’s current functions in one section; edit it to group them however you’d like. It also gitignores the files the build generates.
If your package already has a pkgdown site, most of _pkgdown.yml can be copied over as is; see Coming from pkgdown.
Then build the site:
quartodown::build_site()
In an interactive session, this also opens the site in your browser.
To publish it on GitHub Pages, run quartodown::use_quartodown_action(). It writes a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the site on every push and deploys it to the gh-pages branch.
See Customizing for everything _quartodown.yml can configure.




jlbind

Using quartodown for your package? Feel free to open a pull request adding it to this list.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text: Source: R/use_quartodown_action.R

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Description
Writes .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml, a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the site and deploys it to the gh-pages branch. It runs build_site() on every push, pull request and release, but only deploys when it isn’t a pull request. Also adds ^\.github$ to .Rbuildignore if it’s not already there.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Usage
use_quartodown_action(path = ".", overwrite = FALSE)

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the target package root. Defaults to the current directory.




overwrite


Logical. Replace an existing .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml? By default it’s left as is.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Details
Once the workflow’s first run has created the gh-pages branch, go to the Pages section of the repository’s settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that branch.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to the workflow file.

title: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the site
text:
Examples

pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_quartodown_action(pkg)
#> ✔ Wrote /tmp/RtmpaF9gwX/examplepkg19477ff0dea0/.github/workflows/quartodown.yaml.
#> ✔ Added `^\.github$` to /tmp/RtmpaF9gwX/examplepkg19477ff0dea0/.Rbuildignore.
#> 
#> Next steps:
#> 1. Commit and push the workflow.
#> 2. Once its first run has created the `gh-pages` branch, go to the Pages
#> section of the repository's settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that
#> branch.
list.files(pkg, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE)
#> [1] ".github/workflows/quartodown.yaml" ".Rbuildignore"                    
#> [3] "DESCRIPTION"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)

title: Build the package website
text: Source: R/build_site.R

title: Build the package website
text:
Description
Builds the package website into docs/ with Quarto.

title: Build the package website
text:
Usage
build_site(
  path = ".",
  tooltips = TRUE,
  freeze = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE,
  devel = FALSE,
  preview = interactive()
)

title: Build the package website
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the package root.




tooltips


Logical. Link references to the package’s own functions (in code blocks and inline code) to their reference page, with a hover tooltip showing the function’s usage and the first sentence of its description?




freeze


Logical. Reuse the results of code that ran in an earlier build, for pages whose source hasn’t changed since? Uses Quarto’s freeze, which keeps them in _quarto/_freeze/.




quiet


Logical. Hide Quarto’s rendering output?




devel


Logical. By default, the examples and vignettes run against the package installed from path into a temporary library. With devel = TRUE, they run against it loaded with pkgload::load_all() instead, which is faster, but code that starts other R processes (e.g. with callr or parallel workers) won’t find the package there.




preview


Logical. Open the built site in a web browser with preview_site()? By default, only in interactive sessions.

title: Build the package website
text:
Details
build_site() assembles a Quarto website project in _quarto/ from the package sources and _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, then renders it. It uses README.md (or, without one, DESCRIPTION), man/, the vignettes (including those in subfolders), NEWS.md, LICENSE/LICENSE.md, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and SUPPORT.md (at the top level or in .github/). See vignette("quartodown") for what the site contains.
While it builds, the environment variable IN_QUARTODOWN is "true", so the package’s examples and vignettes can check identical(Sys.getenv("IN_QUARTODOWN"), "true"). IN_QUARTODOWN_PKG is the name of the package whose site it is, which code shared between packages can check.

title: Build the package website
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to the built site.

title: Build the package website
text:
Configuration
_quartodown/_quartodown.yml is optional; use_quartodown() creates one. It can contain:


url: the site’s address, if it isn’t the first URL in DESCRIPTION that isn’t a source repository.


reference: the sections of the function reference index and the topics each lists, by name or with selectors such as starts_with(). The format is the same as pkgdown’s.


navbar: the items on the navbar’s left and right: keywords such as reference and articles, vignettes, and Quarto navbar items and menus. With style: sidebar, the left items go in a sidebar instead, with a link to every reference page.


home: file, the .md or .qmd file the home page shows instead of README.md; sidebar, the sidebar’s structure (its sections, in order) and components (sections of your own), or false to show the page as written, without it; and links, added to the sidebar’s links.


authors: by a person’s name, an href to link it and html to replace it; and under sidebar and footer, the roles shown, with before/after text in the sidebar and text in the footer.


repo: the repository’s urls (home, and the prefixes of links to a file, source; an issue, issue; and a user, user) and branch, if not from DESCRIPTION’s GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg URL.


theme: the light and dark themes: names of Quarto’s built-in themes, such as flatly and darkly, or .scss files in _quartodown/. By default, default and darkly.


redirects: pairs of paths, from an old page to the one replacing it, such as ["reference/old.html", "reference/new.html"].


quarto: settings merged over the generated Quarto configuration.


_quartodown/extra.scss and _quartodown/extra.css, if they exist, style every page, on top of quartodown’s theme. The whole _quartodown/ folder is copied into the Quarto project, so quarto settings can refer to other files in it by the same path.
See vignette("customizing", package = "quartodown") for the details.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Description
Writes _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, the configuration file build_site() reads. It starts with a reference: field listing every function currently documented in <path>/man/*.Rd in one "All functions" section. Also adds the .gitignore/.Rbuildignore entries the build needs (see Details) if they’re not already there.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Usage
use_quartodown(path = ".")

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Arguments



path


Path to the target package root. Defaults to the current directory.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Details
An existing _quartodown.yml is never overwritten.
use_quartodown() adds the following lines to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore (only the ones not already present in each file):

# .gitignore
_quarto/*
!_quarto/_freeze/

# .Rbuildignore
^docs$
^_quarto$
^_quartodown$


_quarto/ is the Quarto project build_site() generates and renders into docs/. Its _freeze/ directory holds the results of code run with build_site(freeze = TRUE), which can be committed so later builds, e.g. on CI, reuse them. _quartodown/ holds the site’s configuration and any files it uses, such as extra.scss.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Value
Invisibly, the path to _quartodown/_quartodown.yml.

title: Set up a package to use quartodown
text:
Examples

pkg <- tempfile("examplepkg")
dir.create(pkg)
write(
  "Package: examplepkg\nVersion: 0.0.0.9000",
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
use_quartodown(pkg)
#> ✔ Wrote /tmp/RtmptCrMZF/examplepkg19296e728a91/_quartodown/_quartodown.yml (edit this to group your functions).
#> ✔ Added `_quarto/*` and `!_quarto/_freeze/` to /tmp/RtmptCrMZF/examplepkg19296e728a91/.gitignore.
#> ✔ Added `^docs$`, `^_quarto$`, and `^_quartodown$` to /tmp/RtmptCrMZF/examplepkg19296e728a91/.Rbuildignore.
#> 
#> Next steps:
#> 1. Edit _quartodown/_quartodown.yml to group your functions the way you want.
#> 2. Build and preview the site with `quartodown::build_site()`.
readLines(file.path(pkg, "_quartodown", "_quartodown.yml"))
#>  [1] "# Configuration for quartodown::build_site(). See"                         
#>  [2] "# vignette(\"customizing\", package = \"quartodown\") for all fields,"     
#>  [3] "# including `navbar:` (navbar items and menus) and `quarto:` (other Quarto"
#>  [4] "# settings)."                                                              
#>  [5] ""                                                                          
#>  [6] "# Groups the function reference index into sections, each with a `title:`" 
#>  [7] "# and the `contents:` it lists (topic names or selectors such as"          
#>  [8] "# starts_with(\"read_\"))."                                                
#>  [9] "reference:"                                                                
#> [10] "  - title: All functions"                                                  
#> [11] "    contents:"                                                             
#> [12] "      []"
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)

Source: vignettes/articles/showcase.qmd
quartodown renders every page with Quarto itself, so all of Quarto’s authoring features work in your vignettes and articles. This page shows some of them as they look on a quartodown site.

title: Quarto features
text:
Callouts






Note



Callouts draw attention to a piece of text. There are five types: note, tip, important, warning and caution.








TipTip with a title



Give a callout a title with a heading as its first line.








WarningClick to expand





Callouts can be collapsible, which is handy for details most readers can skip.

aggregate(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars, FUN = mean)
#>   cyl      mpg
#> 1   4 26.66364
#> 2   6 19.74286
#> 3   8 15.10000

Functions from this package are linked to their reference page, with a tooltip on hover, both inline, like build_site(), and in code:

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Source: vignettes/quartodown.qmd
quartodown builds a website for an R package with Quarto. This guide sets up a package, builds its site, and publishes it on GitHub Pages.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Set up
From the root of your package, run:
quartodown::use_quartodown()
This writes _quartodown/_quartodown.yml, and adds the files the build generates to .gitignore and .Rbuildignore. _quartodown.yml is where you can customize your site. If your package already has a _pkgdown.yml, see Coming from pkgdown for how its settings carry over.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Build the site
quartodown::build_site()
build_site() builds the site into docs/ and, in an interactive session, opens it in your browser. The page reloads when you rebuild, and preview_site() opens it again if you’ve closed it. Examples and vignettes run against your package’s current source. While iterating, build_site(devel = TRUE) is faster because it loads the package with pkgload::load_all() instead of installing it.
The following is added to your site:

Home page: your README.md. Next to it, a sidebar links to the source code, the bug tracker and CRAN (if the package is there), and shows the license, citation and authors from DESCRIPTION. Any badges in your README (between <!-- badges: start --> and <!-- badges: end -->) are moved into the sidebar.
Reference: a page for each help topic in man/, plus an index page listing them all.
Get started: the vignette with the same name as your package, like this one.
Articles: all your other vignettes, including any in subfolders such as vignettes/articles/.
Changelog: your NEWS.md. Issue numbers like #123 and GitHub usernames like @user become links.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Publish on GitHub Pages
To build the site and deploy it to the gh-pages branch on every push, add a GitHub Actions workflow:
quartodown::use_quartodown_action()
This writes .github/workflows/quartodown.yaml. Commit and push it. Once its first run has created the gh-pages branch, go to the Pages section of your repository’s settings on GitHub and choose to deploy from that branch.

title: Get started with quartodown
text:
Learn more
Customizing your site covers everything _quartodown.yml can change.
Quarto features shows Quarto’s authoring features, such as callouts, tabsets and footnotes, on a quartodown site.
Technical details explains how a build works.
